term: indexed route and exhaustive failure consequence
definition: For premise family premises : I → Prop, Complete premises means ∀ i, premises i; Failure premises means ∃ i, ¬premises i. EveryFailureEntails premises X means ∀ i, ¬premises i → X. Empty-index routes are complete and cannot fail. Failure implies incompleteness constructively; conversely incompleteness supplies a failure under the explicit ExcludedMiddle premise. A route is a conjunction in a fixed interpretation, not a measure of philosophical plausibility. RootFromJointFailureIncompatibility quantifies over two such families, a common conclusion and their failure consequences; it is a logical pattern only.
note: Analyst logical rule template requested in #1119. Indices may be finite premise rosters but no finiteness assumption is needed. Common semantic profile and valid route/failure consequence certificates are obligations of every philosophical instantiation. No source attribution or real-world relation is introduced. A counterexample with Bool premises shows that checking one sampled failure implication is insufficient; a shared-obligation theorem shows that covering two routes does not evade any proposition required by both.
